title: A Chiral Superlattice Route to Spin-Split Topological Antiferromagnetism
authors: Thao Dinh, Mengke Liu, Jian-Xiang Qiu, Sougata Mardanya, Suk Hyun Sung, Xuan Hoang Le, Christopher Broyles, Chengfeng Zhu, Qiaozhi Xu, Haotian Chen, Zack Rehfuss, Yu-Fei Liu, Xiaoyu Zeng, Houchen Li, Peng Guo, Jinchen Liu, Tianye Huang, Jingtian Shi, Michael Smith, Joanna M. Blawat, John Singleton, Ross McDonald, Ivan E. Arvizo, Dongtao Cui, Shao-Liang Zheng, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Vineet Kumar Sharma, Sudip Ghorai, Barun Ghosh, Hsin Lin, Ting Yong Lim, Tay-Rong Chang, Arun Bansil, Ivar Martin, Ashvin Vishwanath, Weiwei Xie, Claudia Felser, Jairo Sinova, Anyuan Gao, Mikhail D. Lukin, Jennifer E. Hoffman, Sugata Chowdhury, Qiong Ma, Kai Sun, Ismail El Baggari, Sheng Ran, Talieh S. Ghiasi, Hongkun Park, Philip Kim, Su-Yang Xu
abstract: The interplay between chirality and magnetism is a profound topic, spanning particle physics, condensed matter, chemistry and origin of life. In this paper, we study this interplay in the new antiferromagnet (AFM) UOTe, and we report a chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological phenomena from collinear antiferromagnetism. Pristine UOTe is a collinear AFM without Berry curvature or spin-split bands. However, we identify the spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe, which can be viewed as frozen chiral phonons at finite wave vector. When electrons move through the chiral superlattice, their orbital Bloch wavefunction and quantum geometry are modulated by the strong chiral superlattice potential, generating large Berry curvature in the chiral superlattice, which we detect by the nonlinear Hall effect. At 150 K, the chiral superlattice induced Berry curvature couples to the collinear AFM order, generating a giant anomalous Hall angle ~0.14 abruptly near $T_N$ that is among the largest in bulk magnets. Moreover, our spin Hanle precession measurement shows that the chiral superlattice also generates spin-polarized current from the collinear AFM, a long-standing goal in spintronics. We shed light on the supermodulation formation mechanism based on chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, using which we propose a design principle to discover similar bond-mismatch superlattices, providing a chiral superlattice pathway through real space engineering of quantum geometry.
summary: This work reports discovering a chiral superlattice in the antiferromagnet UOTe, which acts as a structural template to induce topological electronic properties. By coupling this structural chirality to the intrinsic antiferromagnetism, the authors demonstrate the generation of a large anomalous Hall effect and spin-polarized current. This establishes a general design principle for engineering quantum geometry in real materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the interplay between chirality and magnetism to achieve spin-split topological phenomena in an antiferromagnet.
main_result: The spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe generates a large Berry curvature dipole, leading to a giant anomalous Hall angle and spin-polarized current.
method: The study combines experimental techniques (TEM, NLH effect, spin Hanle precession) with theoretical modeling (DFT, tight-binding) to link structural chirality to topological electronic responses.
model_or_system: The system is the antiferromagnet UOTe, which spontaneously develops a chiral superlattice structure due to bond-mismatch effects. This structure modulates the electronic Bloch wavefunction, leading to topological properties.
key_observables: Giant anomalous Hall angle (~0.14), finite Berry curvature dipole (detected by NLH effect), and measurable spin-polarized current via Hanle precession.
important_parameters: Temperature near the Néel temperature ($T_N$), superlattice wavevector ($\vec{q}$), and the energy competition between interlayer and intralayer bonding.
main_assumptions: The superlattice formation is driven by chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, leading to a bond-mismatch mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural confirmation of the superlattice via atomic displacements, the generation of Berry curvature via the nonlinear Hall effect, and the resulting anomalous Hall and spin-polarized transport signals.
paper_structure: The argument progresses from identifying the structural superlattice $ightarrow$ demonstrating its symmetry-breaking, chiral nature $ightarrow$ linking this structural feature to the generation of Berry curvature and topological magnetic responses (AHE, spin current).
why_interesting: The explicit connection between real-space structural engineering (superlattice formation) and the emergence of quantized topological responses (Berry curvature, AHE) provides a powerful, chemically tunable pathway for realizing exotic quantum states.
